$comment: THE DBIZ APPLICATION ROLES, AS A DEPLOYABLE ARTEFACT.
These roles belong to the solution, not to whoever last clicked through the Azure portal. The
role vocabulary is defined in code — ENTRA_ROLE_MAP in
packages/tenant-onboarding-engine/src/engine/microsoft-auth.ts — and the API refuses any identity
whose directory role is not in that closed table. Until this file existed, the vocabulary lived
ONLY in TypeScript: nothing declared the roles for provisioning and nothing created them, so every
deployment had to reproduce them by hand from prose. That is how an environment reaches production
with the role check enabled and no role to satisfy it.
'id' values are STABLE. Azure keys assignments by role id, so regenerating them orphans every
existing assignment. Never change an id; add a new role instead.
'value' is what Entra puts in the token's `roles` claim and is the ONLY field the API matches.
The display name is for humans and is matched by nothing.
Apply with deploy/azure/provision-entra-app-roles.sh. Kept in sync with the code table by

appRoles.description: Global administrator of the Intelligence Plane. Onboards and manages every tenant, issues Execution Plane credentials, and publishes updates. Carries no tenant scope because it is not confined to one.

Administers only the tenants granted by group membership (DBIZ_GROUP_TENANT_MAP). An unmapped group grants no tenant at all, so this role is useless until the mapping exists — deliberately, so scope is never assumed.
Read-only access to tenant configuration and status. Makes no changes.
